articleTitle: A Reliable Antenna Array for the 28GHz mmWave Band in a 5G Massive MIMO Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The high communication performance specifications of the 5G wireless cellular communication standards require electronic components that can reliably support such standards. One such component is the antenna. The antenna is one of the most useful components in wireless communication, and hence, its performance heavily influences the performance of a wireless communication system. In this study, we propose a planar 10×10 microstrip patch antenna (MPA) array for a 5G massive multiple inputs multiple outputs (mMIMO) wireless communication. The antenna was designed and simulated using Pathwave Advanced Design System (ADS), and it achieves a gain of 21.97dBi, radiation efficiency of 0.93, bandwidth of 0.45GHz, and beamwidth of 0.76rad on the 28GHz millimeter wave (mmWave) band of 5G mMIMO communication.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Congestion Control for QUIC in Asymmetrical Latency Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Various networks will be integrated with conventional terrestrial networks in the Beyond 5G (B5G) era, for example, non-terrestrial networks with high latency. In this case, the one-way delay of downlink or uplink might be asymmetrical with a broad range. Meanwhile, QUIC is promising as an efficient scheme based on user datagram protocol (UDP)-enhanced at the transport layer for mobile communications. For a comprehensive investigation, a QUIC testbed is developed based on a wired connection and traffic control command in Linux to emulate the asymmetrical latency environment. This paper reports the results of the performance evaluation of congestion control algorithms for QUIC with the QUIC testbed. The experimental results of throughputs suggest that the research and development to improve the Bottleneck Bandwidth Round-trip propagation time congestion control is very promising for QUIC in the B5G.

articleTitle: Closed-Loop Security Management for Developing O-RAN Infrastructure and B5G RIC Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The emergence of 5G instigates a profound transition towards an open architecture in telecommunications, allowing a diverse array of companies to engage in equipment manufacturing and creating a mutually beneficial business model. Utilizing the principles of Software Defined Networking (SDN) and virtualization, this open architecture constructs key O-RAN components such as base stations, central units, distributed units, radio units, service management orchestration, and RIC applications. However, the widespread integration of software and virtualization into open RANs inevitably leads to an influx of open-source projects without sufficient security validation, posing significant cybersecurity management and development risks. To counter these risks and facilitate the successful commercialization of ORAN, this paper introduces a novel cybersecurity management solution. Adhering to the O-RAN standards and employing a closed-loop management approach, this solution is designed to significantly mitigate the heightened cybersecurity risks linked with open-source projects under the O-RAN framework. Our experimental results substantiate that this solution can effectively identify existing Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) risks in open-source projects, whilst providing timely alerts for potential future cybersecurity threats.

articleTitle: On Manipulating Routing Table to Realize Redirect Attacks in O-RAN by Malicious xApp
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) collaborates through Radio Access Network Intelligent Controllers (RICs) and their associated xAPPs to collect real-time status information from underlying RAN components. This allows dynamically changing the system resources to optimize the RAN's overall performance. Unfortunately, there's no auditing mechanism for xAPP uploads and no adherence to proper permission management protocols. In this article, we implement a working O-RAN platform and discover that the lack of mutual authentication mechanisms between services in the Near-Real-Time RIC and the improper permission settings for xAPPs pose a serious threat. By altering the original routing table and launching redirection attacks, malicious xAPPs could exploit this vulnerability and render the entire RAN inoperable. We provide a detailed report on how the attack was carried out and the impact it caused.

articleTitle: Symphony of Sensors: The Harmonious Art of Massive Data Generation by Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: In today's interconnected world, devices of all shapes and sizes orchestrate a grand symphony of data generation, producing an unparalleled cacophony of information that prevail through every aspect of our lives. This paper takes center stage to explore the intricate choreography of this symphony, shedding light on the diverse cast of devices, the rhythms of data generation, and the significant implications for society. Through a harmonious blend of analysis and imagination, we unravel the melodies of innovation, challenges, and opportunities that arise from the massive data generation by devices.

articleTitle: A CNN-Based Routing Scheme for Minimizing TCP Flow Completion Time in SD-DCNs
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Data centers play a vital role in supporting the increasing demand from the six-generation (6G) networks for cloud services, big data, artificial intelligence and other data-intensive tasks. Software-defined data center networks (SD-DCNs) represent a natural evolution of traditional data center architectures aimed at improving network utilization. In this paper, we consider routing optimization for minimizing the completion time of transmission control protocol (TCP) flows in SD-DCNs. Specifically, we propose a routing scheme based on convolutional neural networks (CNN). Under different traffic transmission scenarios in SD-DCNs, the simulation results show that the flow completion time (FCT) of our scheme is much shorter compared to the equal-cost multipath (ECMP) and the shortest path first (SPF) algorithm, particularly in scenarios involving high-demand applications.

articleTitle: Packet-Level Index Modulation Under Duty Cycle Constraints
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Low power wide area (LPWA) is an important technology in the field of the Internet-of-Things (IoT) because of its low cost and long-distance transmission capability. In LPWA, including LoRa, which is one of its standards, the transmission time per channel is limited by the duty cycle (DC) at each terminal. Thus, packet-level index modulation (PLIM) has been proposed to increase the number of bits. PLIM can transmit additional data by mapping information bits on the time and frequency axes in addition to LoRa transmission. However, if the transmit bit sequence is not i.i.d, a transmitter may continue to choose particular frequency channels, making the transmission on those frequency channels impossible due to DC constraints. To avoid the intensive use of certain frequency channels in PLIM, this paper proposes to adaptively change indexes on the frequency axis. Each LoRa terminal decides the index exchange at regular intervals. A LoRa terminal predicts its transmission occupancy time on each frequency channel based on the transmission history up to the decision period. If the difference between the predicted maximum and minimum transmission time on frequency channels exceeds a predetermined threshold value, the LoRa terminal exchange indexes between the two frequency channels. The simulation results show that the proposed method can avoid the intensive use of specific channels and reduce the untransmittable packets due to DC constraints.

articleTitle: A Novel Random Access for Ultra-Low Latency Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Under the same network topology as the IEEE 802.11be multi-link operation medium access control, we propose an uplink random access that achieves ultra-low latency communication. To support real-time applications (RTAs), packets shall be transmitted immediately without the need of channel sensing or retransmission. In our proposed uplink multiple access, each transmitting station sends <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> uncoded copies of the same packet in parallel on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> random channels across multiple frequency bands. Transmission is considered successful if at least one copy is received without collision. We evaluate the performance for both finite and infinite number of stations using a mathematical model to determine the likelihood of successful transmission. We compare static and adaptive number of copies for finite number of stations case. The adaptive model, which adjusts based on traffic rates, is more efficient, increasing reliability and throughput. The overall performance of the proposed system is subject to traffic density. To ensure sustained performance and reliability, we recommend stabilization by controlling the transmission probability to achieve the desired level of reliability.

articleTitle: Multiple Access Technology Using Long-Range Wide-Angle Array Antennas Mounted on High Altitude Platform Station
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This paper discusses a high altitude relay system of command and telemetry links for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) deployed at lower altitude in wide area. We propose and design a multiple access scheme in space, frequency, and time domains to use the same frequency band for the user and feeder links by employing a multi-beam digital beamforming antenna on board to the high altitude platform station (HAPS). We evaluated the proposed method by conducting experiments using an aircraft. From the experimental results, we verified the effectiveness of the proposed multiple connection scheme by using multibeam when two ground stations are placed in different cells and the simultaneous connection of a ground station and a terminal station in the same cell by time division and frequency division.

articleTitle: C5 and Human Design-A Holistic Approach to Support Childhood Development and Personalization
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: We are living in a dynamic and challenging world today, where our post - modern, techno-science, globalized society calls for increased efficiency, innovation, and better standard of living. The responsibility for this demand lies upon education as investment in Human Capital, which are our children. The need for an educational system that supports raising and educating creative, efficient, and balanced future adults is vitally important. This paper presents C5 (Creativity, Contentment, Confidence, Calmness, Concentration) concept that will help pedagogues, teachers, and parents to unlock children's potential and create a more favorable environment for harmonic, holistic childhood development. In addition, we suggest the Human Design approach be used as a tool to achieve successfully the five categories of C5 concept. The method is psychological, cognitive, objective, and practical that aims to attune to children's universe and to assist them in their personalization, creativity, self-realization, stress management and wellbeing.

articleTitle: Security-Aware Ad Hoc Networking Protocol for Vehicular Safety Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Modern cars are implemented with a number of environmentally-aware safety systems, from radar-induced braking, to oncoming-vehicle detecting headlight controls. Similarly, with the dawn of semi and fully-autonomous vehicles, cars themselves are being equipped with an even wider range of sensors and are able to respond to more stimuli than ever. In this world, inter-vehicular information sharing and vehicle-to-infrastructure communication to exchange road-safety related message is of paramount importance. At the same time, message exchange should conform to standard security goals of authentication, integrity and anonymity. Our proposed system uses a bandwidth-efficient communication protocol which prioritizes message retransmissions by other participating vehicles in a manner that results in low latency and propagation over a wider area on the roadway. Communication between vehicles and RSUs is being protected by pseudo IDs and Hadamard matrix credentials for each vehicle and RSU.

articleTitle: Path Power Prediction Improving Scheme for Millimeter-wave using LSTM under Indoor Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This paper proposes the received power prediction of the first arrival wave in millimeter-wave indoors. The channels are measured assuming that a user walks in a room. The received power of the first arriving wave is obtained from the measured impulse response. The LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) is used for production. The received power at the position ahead of the current position is predicted from the power obtained from the point where the user was previously located. On the other hand, the received power obtained in the experiment is varied because of measurement errors and mismatching between the time of path arrival and sampling point. Therefore, averaging the past several steps is adopted for the training data to reduce the influence of the variation and improve the prediction accuracy. The prediction errors are evaluated to show the effectiveness of the proposed preprocessing scheme.

articleTitle: Cross-Layer Flow Control for Dual-Link Wireless Access of AGV in Factory
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Wireless communication of Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV) is a key feature of modern factories that contribute to achievement of higher productivity. The quality of a wireless link between an AGV and an Access Point (AP) may change drastically during the movement of an AGV. Recently, it has become feasible to use two wireless interfaces devices that can link to different access points to increase robustness of wireless access. Therefore, methods are needed to efficiently coordinate the use of the two interfaces. In this paper, a method is proposed for cross-layer control which splits data flow over two-links based on lower layer information about the estimated flow rate of each link. The method is evaluated by simulation using a flow-level simulation model. Evaluation is done for a particular test scenario of an AGV trip in a factory requiring multiple handovers between APs while transmitting video camera data on an uplink using IEEE 802.11. Simulation results verify that the proposed method is effective in reducing latency of data transmissions to below 100ms and improving stability over the whole range of AGV movement. There results shows that proposed method is effective when the update interval of split ratio is short enough to match the changes of the AP link flow rates due to the movement of AGV.

articleTitle: An Effective Network Topology Coexistence Scheme for the Low-Energy Wireless Grid Structures in the Green Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This paper proposes a network topology coexistence scheme applicable to NICT assuming wireless grid structures that employ low-energy multi-hop frame collection functions and is expected to play a very important role in the future AI-enhanced green communication for sustainable smart cities. The proposed scheme assumes enhanced employment of the existing IEEE 802.15.4g/4e SUN standard with suitable customizations. In the proposed scheme, active period allocation procedures accompanied with SUN association functions are effectively exploited and multiple active periods are actively allocated in order to reduce interferences among network topologies by further considering interference caused by offered frame itself. Computer simulation confirm that the proposed coexistence scheme prevents coexistence performance degradation and show 200 % improvement in the successful coexistence probability. Furthermore, the paper shows the possible implementation of the proposed scheme on the SUN radio devices that were efficiently utilized in the AI-enhanced green communication evaluations.

articleTitle: User Pairing Method Using Radio Map for Spectrum Sharing Between Non-Terrestrial Networks and Terrestrial Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: With the proliferation of the Internet-of-Things (IoT) and cell phones, there is a need to provide high-speed communications to a large number of users. Next-generation mobile communication systems, Beyond 5G/6G, are considering the use of non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) to ensure a wide coverage area and to accommodate the increase in users. Satellite communications, which is one of NTNs, have a wider coverage area than base stations of terrestrial networks (TNs), but utilization of NTNs concerns the impact on terrestrial networks when considering spectrum between NTNs and TNs. For spectrum sharing with the TNs, frequency bands are allocated for each communication link, and an investigation is conducted on the timing schedule method for TNs and NTNs terminals. We consider the impact on each terminal and base station when using reverse pairing, which reverses the up-link and down-link frequency resource links between NTNs and TNs. In addition, a radio map that stores information on radio propagation in space for wireless communication is used for calculating the interference between systems. To avoid interference between terminals, which was found to be necessary when performing reverse pairing, scheduling of terminals is conducted, and a radio map is utilized for this schedule. We simulate and evaluate the permissible number of spectrum shared terminals for terrestrial networks without interference toward terminals of NTNs, which is affected by the error of the information of the radio map. The results show that the spectrum database using a radio map can increase the number of spectrum shared terminals for terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks if the estimation error of received signal power is within 7 [dB].

articleTitle: Multi Stage Log-Likelihood Ratio Estimation with Ordering in a Non-Linear Receiver for Overloaded MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This paper proposes multi stage log-likelihood ratio (LLR) estimation in a non-linear overloaded MIMO receiver with soft-input decoding. The proposed technique can reduce the computational complexity of the LLR estimation. Furthermore, we propose ordered LLR estimation, which improves the transmission performance with negligible small additional complexity. The performance of the receiver with the multi stage and ordered LLR estimation is confirmed by computer simulation in a 6 × 3 MIMO-OFDM system. The non-linear receiver achieves almost the same transmission performance to the conventional soft-input maximum likelihood detector (MLD) receiver, even though the complexity of the receiver with the proposed LLR estimation is about one-third as much as that of the soft-input MLD. The complexity can be further reduced to one-tenth of that of the soft-input MLD, if about 1.0 dB performance degradation at the BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−5</sup> is acceptable.

articleTitle: SDR-based 5G NR System Verification with Video Transmission for Wireless Emulator
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The Society 5.0 will be strongly assisted by cyber-physical systems (CSP) with collecting various data in a physical space, analyzing them in a cyber space, and actuating physical devices. To harness the full potential of CPS across diverse societal and industrial realms, the establishment of an advanced and robust wireless communication infrastructure is needed. The forthcoming evolution embodied by Beyond 5G (B5G) holds promise for achieving these objectives, while the realization of such technologies requires field trials that are essential for practical implementation. However, as systems become more enhanced and larger in scale, the cost and time for field trials also escalate, making early practical implementation more challenging. The authors are currently developing a wireless emulator that can be used for development and verification of such new technologies in a cyber space. This kind of virtual evaluation and verification platform is expected to significantly reduce the time and effort required for field trials, and then, can accelerate R&D of new wireless communication technologies. Furthermore, it can accelerate interference recognition and control technologies and spectrum sharing technologies for the purpose of coexistence with other systems. This paper reports on the developed evaluation environment for 5G NR using software-defined radio (SDR) devices and describes the results of system verification, including a video transmission system.

articleTitle: Indoor and Outdoor Measurement Campaign for Unlicensed 6 GHz Operation with Wi-Fi 6E
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The current Wi-Fi frequency bands (2.4 and 5 GHz bands) are severely congested due to the exponential growth of Wi-Fi-enabled devices with the increasing demands of higher capacity and faster wireless connections. Wi-Fi 6E is a potential solution to meet these needs by employing channels of up to 160 MHz bandwidth in the 6 GHz unlicensed band. However, there is limited research on understanding the effect of Wi-Fi 6E on incumbent users of the band. With this motivation, we conduct a comprehensive measurement campaign for a typical real-world deployment of Wi-Fi 6E Low Power Indoor (LPI) Access Points (APs) in a building. The campaign consists of both walking and fixed location measurements to evaluate outdoor beacon Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI), outdoor channel connectivity, and building entry loss (BEL) at 6 GHz band. The measurement results demonstrate outdoor RSSI level ranging from -64 dBm to -95 dBm with a median of -89 dBm, median outdoor downlink (DL) throughput level of 25 Mbps, and 25–33 dB BEL due to solid brick walls. We conclude that (i) outdoor RSSI levels do note pose a threat to incumbent fixed links and (ii) construction material plays a vital role on outdoor RSSI with highest levels observed immediately in front of glass doors and windows.

articleTitle: Inter-Slot Frequency Hopping with DMRS Bundling for NR Coverage Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Coverage performance promotion is crucial for operators when commercializing wireless networks, to this end, enhancement based on inter-slot frequency hopping with demodulation reference signal (DMRS) bundling was introduced and standardized in 3GPP, where frequency hopping in unit of slot-bundle is enabled. However, existed hopping pattern may result in an unbalanced slots distribution between different frequency positions that causes performance degradation. In this paper, we present and analyze a modified hopping pattern, which involves the system frame number in determining the hopping position. The proposed pattern has very small standardization impact but can effectively address the unbalanced issue. The performance gain of the modified hopping pattern is validated by link-level simulation, where about 0.7 dB gain can be observed in some typical case.

Author Keywords: inter-slot frequency hopping with DMRS bundling

articleTitle: Validation of a CommSense Based ISAC System Using In-Situ mmWave Propagation Model
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: With the imminent arrival of sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks, conventional communication-centric systems face challenges in meeting future demands. As transformative technologies need real-time and reliable sensing capabilities, Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) emerges as a comprehensive framework, integrating communication and sensing functionalities in one system. Sensing the environment using the information from channel equalization, called Communication based Sensing (CommSense), has been an area of investigation by the authors for more than a decade. In this work, we validate a CommSense-based ISAC system using insitu mmWave propagation models. To do this, firstly, we verify the accuracy of our real-world measurements by validating the measured Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) against a standard path loss model for the 60GHz band. Secondly, we derive an in-situ Cluster Delay Line (CDL) channel model by simulation, leveraging real map data to accurately represent dynamic wireless environments. Finally, we apply CommSense using the derived CDL channel and observe that it achieves good accuracy in real-time environmental sensing. The result is the facilitation of adaptive and context-aware communication strategies, enabling transformative applications such as intelligent traffic management, environmental monitoring, and IoT. Through our contributions, we demonstrate the potential of CommSense in achieving accurate sensing performance, opening avenues for the future of wireless networks.

articleTitle: Fundamental Field Experiments of OFDMA Systems Using VHF-band in Urban Area
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: OFDMA mobile communication systems in the VHF band are being studied to achieve transmission speeds of several Mbps while covering an area of several tens of kilometers, which is larger than the current communication area (1–2 km) of cellular systems, and to transmit various control signals and image information for the Internet of Things and Vehicle-to-Everything. In particular, ARIB STD-T103 and IEEE 802.16n are standardized communication systems using OFDMA in the VHF band, and their transmission performance has already been evaluated using computer simulation. Moreover, their performances have been evaluated in laboratory experiments by developing actual radio equipment. This study shows the outdoor transmission characteristics of OFDMA systems operating in the VHF band in an urban area. The evaluations were conducted using OFDMA system with base and mobile stations compliant with ARIB STD-T103 mode 1 and IEEE 802.16n at 195 MHz. It was demonstrated that error-free transmission was achieved over an area of approximately 10 km, even in a line-of-sight mobile environment.

articleTitle: Standardizing Personal Medical Data in 5G and 6G Era
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Electronic health records (EHR) are crucial for facilitating comprehensive and efficient patient care, enabling seamless information sharing among healthcare providers and enhancing clinical decision-making. Growing use of smart wearables and home automation devices with embedded sensors has created numerous opportunities for developing novel high-quality solutions in many sectors, including eHealth. The potential of using user-collected health data is enormous in the 5G and 6G era, making it a paradigm that holds promise for improving people's health and wellbeing. A step closer to ensuring continuous healthcare access would be achieved if EHRs were equipped to store and interpret data collected by sensors. This would result in standard-compliant personalized medical services. This paper presents the process of standardizing the data by defining semantic constraints for healthcare data types and modeling a procedure for validating the obtained data ensuring compliance to relevant standards and regulations.

articleTitle: MQTT Protocol Based IoT Solution for Voice-Controlled Smart Home
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This paper proposes an Internet of Things (IoT) solution for a voice-controlled smart home. The smart home is the basic building block of a smart city, in which the smart devices are connected to the cloud enabling that the user controls them remotely. The next generation of smart homes moves toward voice-controlled automation where the voice command eliminates the need for physically operating home electronic appliances. In the proposed solution, the message queuing telemetry transport (MQTT) protocol is used in the transport of data through the IoT network. Further, the Adafruit IO server is used as an MQTT broker. The users need to provide the voice commands via the Google Assistant app installed on mobile phones, which is being converted to meaningful instruction of operation by using suitable applets in IF-THIS-THEN-THAT (IFTTT) that publish it in the appropriate feed of the broker. The endpoint embedded devices subscribe to the instruction to operate the appliances.

articleTitle: A Lite-SVM Based Semantic Search Model for Bigdata Analytics in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The distributed file system used by conventional concepts of big data lacks the extra security and privacy features, which are required more time and energy wastage. In this research, propose a methodology for managing private and safe big data modeling with LITE SVM-based semantic application. It's not possible to scale the big data platform, and there's no assurance of security and time scaling. The suggested technique uses an SVM machine to accurately address these concerns without compromising either security or privacy and without affecting the energy consumption of the application. The main objective of this research is, to manage the Bigdata platform with effective storage in less Time of Conversion (ToC). The existing models like Genetic Algorithm (GA), Differential Annealing (DE) for global optimization, and Fuzzy models were limited to functioning. So that to crossover the above limitations proposed Lite SVM machine learning techniques. The accuracy 82.23%, true positive rate 98.23%, recall 84.53%, & F1 score 92.34% were observed with suggested Lite SVM and compared with past techniques. Such new and enhanced SVM method outcomes are competitive with the most recent methods.

articleTitle: Network-Independent and User-Controlled RIS: An Experimental Perspective
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The march towards 6G is accelerating and future wireless network architectures require enhanced performance along with significant coverage especially, to combat impairments on account of the wireless channel. Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) technology is a promising solution, that has recently been considered as a research topic in standards, to help manipulate the channel in favor of users' needs. Generally, in experimental RIS systems, the RIS is either connected to the transmitter (Tx) or receiver (Rx) through a physical backhaul link and it is controlled by the network and requires significant computation at the RIS for codebook (CB) designs. In this paper, we propose a practical user-controlled RIS system that is isolated from the network to enhance communication performance and provide coverage to the user based on its location and preference. Furthermore, a low-complexity algorithm is proposed to aid in CB selection for the user, which is performed through the wireless cloud to enable a passive and energy efficient RIS. Extensive experimental test-bed measurements demonstrate the enhanced performance of the proposed system while both results match and validate each other.

articleTitle: Interpolation Accuracy Evaluation for 3D Radio Environment Maps Construction
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The characterization of the wireless spectrum in modern and future communications has been established as an important field of research, particularly in view of the increasing densification of terrestrial and aerial network nodes. Radio Environment Maps (REMs) have been prominently utilized for volumetric spectrum occupancy analysis and the design of algorithms for resource allocation but their construction relies on interpolation methods due to the limited availability of measurements. This paper evaluates four such estimators for two datasets collected in real-world environments in three-dimensional (3D) space - indoor through an automated measuring tool, and outdoor through a UAV-based sensor. The process of calibration of the interpolation methods is described, and their performance is assessed, reaching a minimum error of −7 dB. The influence of the distance between the measurement points and the estimated ones, on the accuracy, is analyzed. The findings in this work facilitate the further analysis in 3D signal propagation and REM prediction.

articleTitle: Slicing 5G Core Network Based on the Ryu SDN Controller for Everything as a Service
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: SDN has brought a high level of programmability in networking technologies and plays a vital role for the development of 5G and beyond 5G systems. As a major novel concept associated with SDN, network slicing enables the creation of virtual networks with distinct control and management functions based on common infrastructure, each meeting specific requirements that are dedicated to various categories of applications. So far, the realization of network slicing based on complex frameworks like management and orchestration has been a popular approach. In this paper, we investigate a lightweight alternative method for implementing network slicing that allocates logical parts of multiple physical resources with certain QoS properties without the need for hypervisor software. The approach herein is to create slices at the SDN forwarding equipment level and a single SDN controller can configure a shared physical network infrastructure into a number of network slices. Using this method, each slice may have different properties depending on the tenant requirements. In particular, a resource reservation framework and special Linux kernel tools are used for resource reservation and allocation. This solution offers several benefits for tenants and service providers thanks to the involvement of already available kernel mechanisms for resource allocation. In our implementation, several tools such as Iperf for traffic generation, Linux Cgroup and linear rate control, Ryu controller, and Mininet are included. Through experiments performed based on our implementation, we demonstrate that performance isolation has been achieved successfully for each slice.

articleTitle: Radar Sensing in OFDM Systems with Bandwidth Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Radar sensing is a key envisioned feature in next generations of wireless systems, which allows using communication infrastructure and air interface components to also perceive the environment. Enabling efficient use of the radio spectrum to meet various communication and sensing use case requirements, is one of the main goals in such systems. Due to the dependency of sensing detection performance on the radio signal's frequency bandwidth, and the fact that a contiguous wide bandwidth may not be always available, it is important to equip the future wireless systems with techniques to enable high performance sensing over disjoint aggregated bandwidths. This paper introduces sensing receiver techniques to enable both incoherent and coherent sensing processing across disjoint bandwidths and improve sensing range detection performance.

articleTitle: Dynamic Multi-Tenant RAN Slicing for eMBB, URLLC, and mMTC in 5G Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Network slicing is astute to cope with the heterogeneity of 5G services. The multi-service networks require the segregation of the available radio resources into multiple slices. We consider in this paper radio resources that are owned and managed by the mobile network operator (MNO) which dynamically shares the network infrastructure with multiple mobile virtual network operators (MVNOs) and adjusts the necessary radio resources to be used by each deployed network service under dynamic traffic load. We study the problem of enabling the coexistence of the three 5G services eMBB, URLLC, and mMTC altogether. We propose a multi-tenant radio access network (RAN) slicing approach that meets the different quality of service (QoS) requirements of the different services, ensures multi-tenant and multi-service isolation, and maximizes the efficiency of the resource utilization while maintaining operator QoS by using scheduling and game theory. Then, we provide an analytical model that estimates the minimum required resources for the mentioned three services by using tools from queuing theory. Extensive simulations validate the proposed approach's effectiveness compared with the centralized and static schemes. Numerical results show that our proposed model achieves high performance in terms of resource utilization efficiency, improves the sojourn time of the URLLC slice and the data rate of the eMBB slice, and allows large connectivity of IoT devices while maintaining the isolation between the multi-tenants.

articleTitle: Radio Resource Allocation in Low-to Medium-Load Regimes for Energy Minimization With C-RAN
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Radio resource allocation is critical in order to manage available bandwidth and optimize network behavior. In Centralized-Radio Access Networks (C-RAN), simple Radio Units (RUs) are deployed and can be controlled remotely to allow cooperation. In this paper, we consider micro-cell systems with low-to-medium load regimes. We study the resource allocation problem with minimization of the energy consumption due to radio transmission and signal processing. We propose to mix two transmission modes over a reference period allowing resource reuse: one with all RUs transmitting the same signal, the other with each RU transmitting a specific signal. We impose the same target rate for each user equipment (UE), the same transmit power for the RUs, and a maximum resource block (RB) number, which defines the constraints. The resulting optimization problem is formulated so as to be mixed integer linear programming (MILP). Simulations are run using CPLEX Python API and show the efficiency of the proposed scheme to increase the capacity while consuming the least energy. We also observe that the mode with all RUs simultaneously serving the same UE is more efficient (fewer RB and lower consumed energy) than the mode with a single RU activated at a time.

articleTitle: Physical-Layer Authentication Over Spatially Correlated MIMO Channels
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: We propose a novel physical-layer authentication (PLA) method that exploits spatio-temporal correlation features of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channels. In particular, in the proposed method, the correlation due to the spatial structure and aging of the channel between two legitimate nodes (Alice and Bob), captured in the corresponding covariance matrix, is incorporated into the Mahalanobis distance between consecutive channel estimates and utilized to detect the attack by an impersonator. The authentication decision is carried out via hypothesis testing, with distributions and threshold derived analytically. Computer simulations demonstrate that, for a given false alarm probability, the proposed method can detect an attacker with a higher probability than a conventional method based on Euclidean distances between channels.

articleTitle: Research Issues in False Information Broadcasting Rogue Node Detection for Green VANETs
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Vehicular Ad-hoc Networks (VANETs) serve as the basis of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS). Green communication for VANETs emphasizes reducing the harmful impacts of vehicular communication on the environment through energy-efficient communication, reduced fuel consumption, alleviation of road congestions, and reduced emission of harmful compounds, etc. In VANETs, the participating nodes (vehicles) benefit from the broadcasted beacon messages among themselves that can aid in achieving the objectives of green communication. However, a rogue node in this setup may broadcast false information that may lead to potential hazards and nullify the desirable properties of green communication. Hence the detection of such rogue nodes is critical. Different techniques such as cryptography, trust score evaluation, statistical techniques, AI-based methods, etc., are used to detect false information broadcasting rogue nodes. The characteristics of VANETs and the detection of false information broadcasting rogue nodes introduce unique research issues to the problem. In this paper, we discuss these research issues that should be addressed by a technique for detecting false information broadcasting rogue nodes and highlight their importance in fulfilling green communication in VANETs.

articleTitle: Federated Learning with Packet Losses
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This paper tackles the problem of training Federated Learning (FL) algorithms over real-world wireless networks with packet losses. Lossy communication channels between the orchestrating server and the clients affect the convergence of FL training as well as the quality of the learned model. Although many previous works investigated how to mitigate the adverse effects of packet losses, this paper demonstrates that FL algorithms over asymmetric lossy channels can still learn the optimal model, the same model that would have been trained in a lossless scenario by classic FL algorithms like FedAvg. Convergence to the optimum only requires slight changes to FedAvg: i) while FedAvg computes a new global model by averaging the received clients' models, our algorithm, UPGA-PL, updates the global model by a pseudo-gradient step; ii) UPGA-PL accounts for the potentially heterogeneous packet losses experienced by the clients to unbias the pseudo-gradient step. Still, UPGA-PL maintains the same computational and communication complexity as FedAvg. In our experiments, UPGA-PL not only outperforms existing state-of-the-art solutions for lossy channels (by more than 5 percentage points on test accuracy) but also matches FedAvg's performance in lossless scenarios after less than 150 communication rounds.

articleTitle: Towards Transmission Rate Control Considering the Effects of the Surrounding Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: In today's logistics sites, there is a rising trend in employing advanced equipment such as stacker cranes and conveyor robots equipped with wireless LAN devices to reduce labor costs and enhance operational efficiency. However, high-rise warehouses present distinctive challenges to wireless LAN communication due to the arrangement of metal pillars in vertical, horizontal, and diagonal patterns. This structural complexity engenders convoluted radio propagation paths, resulting in unexpected signal attenuation. This paper addresses a data-driven approach to applying propagation models to such environments. Specifically, we measure the direction of arrival and received signal strength indicator (RSSI) at each polarization of a 5-GHz wireless LAN. Subsequently, we expand the propagation model based on the radio characteristics of the high-rise warehouse by analyzing the acquired data. The analysis revealed that nonlinear attenuation, which does not show linear proportionality to distance, is locally intensified by reflected waves emanating from the surrounding metal band. Furthermore, the difference from the simulation results indicates that the accuracy can be improved by considering the leakage power of cross-polarized. By using the extended model to calculate the leakage power of cross-polarized waves at the transmitting and receiving antennas, we successfully enhance the accuracy of transmission rate estimation of wireless LANs from 11% (using the original model) to 87% in the best-case scenario.

articleTitle: Federated Learning Composite Ad Hoc Interference Maps
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Efficient resource allocation is essential for ad hoc wireless networks and is becoming increasingly crucial for massive Machine Type Communication (mMTC). Resource allocation typically requires interference maps maintained either centrally or by each device. Centralized interference maps, used for Access Point (AP)-assisted resource allocation, require the interference between each device to be measured to capture the global interference map, a mammoth combinatorial task considering massive deployments. Unfortunately, the channel estimation overhead is a significant obstacle due to the limited channel coherence duration. On the other hand, while distributed localized interference maps do not incur a high overhead to construct, they only consider local conditions. As such, localized interference maps tend to be suboptimal. This work introduces a novel Federated Learning (FL) approach to interference map generation. Our method enables AP-autonomous resource allocation and is less complex than traditional interference map generation techniques. As a result, it yields a higher per device sum rate than achievable with localized interference mans.

articleTitle: Cramer-Rao Lower Bound Analysis for OTFS and OFDM Modulation Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation as a promising signal representation attracts growing interest for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), yet its merits over orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) remain controversial. This paper devotes to a comprehensive comparison of OTFS and OFDM for sensing from the perspective of Cramér-Rao lower bounds (CRLB) analysis. To this end, we develop the cyclic prefix (CP)-Free and CP-added models for OFDM, while for OTFS, we consider the Zak transform based and the Two-Steps conversion based models, respectively. Then we rephrase these four models into a unified matrix format to derive the CRLB of the delays and Doppler shifts for multipath scenario. Numerical results demonstrate the superiority of OTFS modulation for sensing, and the effect of physical parameters for performance achievement.

articleTitle: Testing Black Boxes: Verification and Validation of AI Models in Wireless Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Fifth generation (5G) cellular communication system provides a flexible system architecture that enables wireless communication technology to penetrate different verticals and connect various devices. Applying machine learning to develop AI models applicable to various application scenarios becomes a promising direction for designing 5G systems. However, developing AI models for wireless communication algorithms brings new challenges to system design and verification. This paper provides an overview of studies on the verification and testing of wireless communication algorithms developed by machine learning methodology. Due to the black-box nature and scenario-specified data-based model development of the machine learning approach, standardization of testing and verification procedures becomes a new challenge when the device under test implements AI models. We explain the general issues in the context of use cases studied by 3GPP standardization group to illustrate how the application of machine learning to wireless communication systems design emerging as a unique problem from the testing and verification perspective. We then summarize the challenges to develop effective testing and verification procedures. Through explaining the issues and challenges, this paper aims to provide a framework for future studies on resolutions to enable wireless communication AI model testing and verification.

articleTitle: Optimal Deep Learning Model for UAVs: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Unmanned Autonomous Vehicles (UAVs), particularly autonomous flying drones, have garnered significant attention in the field of Artificial Intelligence. Advancements in electronic technology, marked by smaller, cheaper, and more efficient components, have led to substantial progress in UAV research. These versatile devices find applications in diverse fields, ranging from flood monitoring and algae spread detection in water bodies to forest trail identification. In this work, we focus on autonomous flying drones, conducting a comprehensive case study to assess the efficiency, robustness, and accuracy of UAVs. Our research is substantiated through a series of experiments, providing a detailed analysis of the software and hardware architecture employed in the study. We present the implementation algorithms and compare three state-of-the-art approaches: TrailNet, InceptionResnet, and MobileNet, in terms of accuracy, robustness, power consumption, and inference time. Our study reveals that MobileNet outperforms the other algorithms, offering superior results with minimal computational requirements and power consumption. Additionally, we address the challenges encountered during our research and discuss potential avenues for enhancing safety features and overall performance in future work.

Index Terms: ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge

articleTitle: Traffic Load Prediction and Power Consumption Reduction for Multi-Band Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Energyis a major expense issue for mobile operators. In the case of wireless networks, base stations have been identified as the main source of energy consumption. In this paper, we study the energy consumption reduction problem based on real measurements for a commercial multi-band LTE network. Specifically, we are interested in sleep modes to turn off certain frequency bands during low traffic periods and consequently reduce power consumption. We determine the number of frequency bands really needed at each time period. The frequency bands that are not needed can be disabled to reduce energy consumption. In order to allow the operator to predict how many bands can be switched off without major impact on the quality of service, we propose to use a deep learning algorithm, such as Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM). Based on the captured data traces, we have shown that the proposed LSTM model can save an average of 8% to 21% of the energy consumption during working days.

articleTitle: Using Authenticated Encryption for Securing Controller Area Networks in Autonomous Mobile Platforms
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Controller Area Networks (CAN) has become the dominant data communication and networking system used in today's smart vehicles, autonomous mobile platforms, and industrial control systems. Although CAN bus, a vehicle bus standard designed to allow microcontrollers and devices to communicate with each other's applications provides robust and reliable internode data communication, existing CAN technology lacks support for secure data communication and data authentication. This paper explores the utilization of a lightweight and power-efficient authenticated data encryption engine based on TinyJAMBU-128. The proposed system is suitable for autonomous mobile platforms with CAN bus capability. In our proposed testbed, CAN data frames transmitted over the bus will be encrypted and authenticated with minimal power consumption using TinyJAMBU-128. We have analyzed the performance of TinyJAMBU-128 against three parameterized data encryption modules: AES-128/192/256, CAMELLIA-128/192/256, and ARIA-128/192/256. Based on our simulation data, CAN frames encrypted and authenticated via TinyJAMBU-128 required 22%, 17%, and 15% less average energy consumption compared to AES, CAMELLIA, and ARIA respectively.

articleTitle: Distributed Multi-Agent Interference Coordination in Native AI Enabled Multi-Cell Networks for 6G
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: As Information, Communications, and Data Technology (ICDT) are deeply integrated, the research of 6G gradually rises. 6G will spark an era featuring ubiquitous intelligence and realize “Native AI”. However, with the large-scale deployment of access points, the diverse application-specific requirements, as well as the highly dynamic wireless environment, interference problems become more complex in 6G, it's of crucial importance to deploy efficient intelligent interference coordination schemes into 6G network. In this paper, we propose a distributed multi-agent interference coordination scheme in native AI enabled multi-cell networks for 6G. Specifically, we exploit the collaboration among 6G intelligent base stations and RAN (Radio Access Network) architecture with endogenous AI to deploy and execute a full lifecycle process of distributed interference management based on multi-agent deep reinforcement learning on the central Unit (CU) and distributed Unit (DU) side, achieving AI enabled network performance optimization, so that the interference coordination agents can adaptively adjust their strategies for the global throughput performance optimum. Numerical results demonstrate that intelligent collaborative interference coordination for 6G can increase the throughput by 9.07% compared with traditional methods.

articleTitle: Hash-Based Function Call Graph Fusion Method for IoT Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) has brought convenience, efficiency, and significant risks, notably malware threats to IoT security. Enhancing security measures and adopting innovative detection strategies are crucial for sustainable IoT development. The Function Call Graph (FCG) is critical for classifying malicious programs. Still, reverse-engineered FCGs often have multiple functions with identical Opcode Sequences, reducing detection accuracy and potential false positives. Previous research on FCG-based malware detection has largely ignored this issue. To address this prevalent issue, the present study proposes a novel approach that leverages the distinctive characteristics of hash functions to enable one-to-one mapping and efficient searching. This method merges nodes within the FCG that share identical opcode sequences, resulting in significantly reduced training and preprocessing times while preserving the detection process's accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate a remarkable 36% reduction in training time, along-side an impressive 99.17% accuracy rate, thereby underscoring the efficacy and practicality of this proposed solution.

articleTitle: Quantum Wireless Imaging and Remote Sensing - State-of-the-Art Technologies and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Quantum entanglement that does not exist in classic world suggests disruptive quantum i<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex>age/sig<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>al processing and wireless sensing techniques beyond the frontier of classic image/signal processing and sensing. By showing the fundamental difference between classic and quantum techniques, this paper comprehensively explains the principles and mechanisms of quantum wireless ghost imaging, quantum radar, and secure quantum remote sensing, with suggestions toward future technological opportunities in communication and signal processing.

articleTitle: User Location Uncertainty in RIS-Aided Channel Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This paper considers an indoor smart radio environment (SRE) where a Base Station (BS) communicates with a set of user equipment (UE) in the sub-THz band by reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs), as the direct BS-UE links are obstructed. Motivated by the sparsity of the sub-THz channel, we model each RIS as an electronically steerable reflector, which can be described by a single parameter, i.e., the steering angle. We focus on the case where the positions of the UEs are unknown and have to be estimated. Specifically, we propose a novel approach to use RISs for jointly localizing the UEs and optimizing the communication performance. The UE localization is made possible by a dedicated RIS and is handled by a machine learning (ML) algorithm, which exploits the signal transmitted by the UEs and received at the BS. Once the estimates of the UE positions are available, the downlink communication between BS and UEs is optimized by properly selecting the electronic steering angle of the RISs so as to maximize the network throughput. By numerical simulations, the paper shows how the system performance is affected by the area of the RISs, by the number of antennas available at the BS, and by the number of steering angles scanned by the RIS used for localization.

articleTitle: Campus-Based Full-Scale and Portable Open-Source 5G SA Networks: Prototyping and Experiments
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: In light of the thrilling development of future mobile communication systems and worldwide 5G deployment, there is a trend toward open-source-based solutions, which could reduce costs, provide flexibility, enable innovation, and expand know-how on 5G RAN and 5G CN operations. In this study, we design and implement two distinct 5G SA open-source-based testbeds. The first network architecture, a Portable Network, comprises a Lenovo laptop used in tandem with a USRP B210. The second network architecture, a Full-Scale Network, is a campus-based 5G network deployed at a lab facility, consisting of a Dell server and a USRP X300. Based on the implementations of these two network architectures, extensive experiments have been performed with a COTS UE connected to the network. Our results provide insight on the performance of such networks with respect to network connectivity and computing performance.

articleTitle: A Computer Aided Design Tool for NISQ Logic Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Computed Aided Design (CAD) is essential to synthesize noisy intermediate scale quantum (NISQ) information and communication systems. The prevailing model for NISQ systems is gate-based and uses logical components arranged into a circuit to represent different quantum operations. A CAD Tool for Quantum Logic is proposed to synthesize gate-based NISQ circuits for computing, communication, or sensing by supplying designers with parameterized versions of common quantum algorithms as well as a design space for simulating photonics hardware implementations. Available in a software package called the CADTQL, designers can test their conventional and optical quantum logic configurations and realize more efficient designs.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Duplex Switching Scheme That Exploits Interference Statistics for Hybrid-Duplex Cellular Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The full duplex (FD) technique allows transmission and reception in the same frequency band and at the same time. It can potentially improve the spectral efficiency. However, in a cellular network, FD communication results in increased interference which may diminish the gain. It has been shown that hybrid designs with proper selection between the FD and the half duplex (HD) modes can reach a performance better than that of the pure FD and pure HD systems. The optimal mode selection requires accurate channel information within a cell and between cells which incur a significant amount of signaling overhead and the computation is highly complex. In this paper, we propose a duplex switching method based on only the instantaneous channel information within a cell and the statistics of the other-cell interference to avoid extensive information exchange and complex computation. The other-cell interference depends on the portions of the links in the other cells adopting the FD or HD mode, which again depend on the other-cell interference these links see. Due to this recursion or interaction between cells, the interference statistics are difficult to derive. Using stochastic geometry, we propose an approximation approach to obtain the probability of other cells adopting the FD mode, and use this probability to approximate the other-cell interference which is then exploited for duplex mode switching in a cell. Simulation results show that the proposed design outperforms the pure FD, pure HD, and an existing duplex switching system. Surprisingly, it also outperforms a system with mode selection based on the actual instantaneous other-cell interference.

articleTitle: GPT for the Metaverse in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The metaverse is a virtual space that blends elements of augmented reality, virtual reality, and many other technologies, offering a tailored and immersive experience where individuals can communicate with each other and digital objects. Though the metaverse incorporates various advanced technologies, there is still room for enhancement in terms of interactivity and in achieving realism of virtual environments. Generative Pre-trained Transformers can help address these issues. GPTs advanced NLP algorithms that generate dynamic and realistic content in real-time, allowing the creation of interactive non-playable characters, improving NLP for chatbots and voice assistants, and generating realistic virtual environments in the metaverse. The integration of GPT and metaverse is essential to make it a more dynamic, realistic, and engaging workspace. This review paper explores the opportunity of integrating GPTs with the metaverse applications and highlights prospective challenges associated with this integration.

articleTitle: Interference Analysis and Mitigation for UAV Communications in Drone Corridors
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have witnessed widespread adoption in the modern world, with their development set to continue into the future. As UAV technology and applications advance, it becomes imperative to understand their communication capabilities. UAVs experience distinct radio propagation conditions compared to ground-based radio nodes, necessitating a critical investigation into aerial radio node performance. This paper analyzes interference in UAV-to-UAV (U2U) communications within drone corridors and proposes an interference mitigation strategy utilizing millimeter wave (mmWave) beamforming. Employing a semi-persistent scheduling approach from the Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) sidelink communications for low altitude aerial nodes in drone corridors, the study primarily examines interference from drone clusters within designated air corridors. To assess U2U communication performance, a 3GPP standard-compliant cross-layer simulator is developed. Simulation results demonstrate that employing mmWave beamforming instead of isotropic transmission substantially reduces interference, leading to higher communications reliability and enabling more UAVs to occupy and communicate in the airspace.

articleTitle: Quantum Computing Technologies to Accelerate 6G and CONASENSE Integration Beyond 2030
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This article underscores the pivotal role of quantum computing and related technologies in advancing Communication, Navigation, Sensing, and Services Integration (CONASENSE) in the 6G realm. The study provides a methodical journey through the chronological development of computing paradigms, starting from foundational computational frameworks like Turing Machines and Von Neumann's architecture, culminating in a sophisticated understanding of Quantum Turing Machines. Tracing computing's evolution from Turing Machines to Quantum Turing Machines, it acknowledges contributions from scientists like Bohr, Einstein, Feynman, and Benioff to quantum theory. The convergence of Quantum Computing and AI offers solutions to complex, NP-hard challenges, heralding a new era of optimization. This includes Quantum Computing, Quantum Algorithms, Quantum Machine Learning (QML), Quantum Communications, Quantum Sensing & Metrology, Quantum Simulation, and Quantum Imaging within the emerging CONASENSE and 6G paradigms, projecting their sustained relevance and impact beyond 2030.

articleTitle: Enhancing Quick Discovery of Neighbor Devices in Distributed D2D With Adaptive Control at Receiver
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Distributed device-to-device (D2D) communication has been gaining attention in recent years. IEEE STD 802.15.8 is an international standard developed for fully distributed D2D. Moreover, 3GPP defines LTE-V2X Mode 4 for distributed D2D without exploiting LTE/5G networks. In absence of central control unit, control functions are executed in a distributed manner. Each device independently contends channel based on CSMA/CA procedure. The possibility of channel congestion increases if the number of neighbor devices is large. When applying distributed D2D communications to flying drones or moving vehicles, congestion may occur dynamically and locally following the movement of PDs. That may deter discovery of neighbor devices. In this paper, we propose an algorithm of adaptive control at receiver for distributed D2D. Each device independently judges if itself falls into congestion situation or not. If congestion occurs, the proposed algorithm enables priority on channel access based on distance between devices so that neighbor devices within short range can be discovered preferentially. We examine the proposed algorithm with multiagent modeling simulations using Netlogo. The simulation results show both improved broadcast ratio and discovery ratio, that verify the effectiveness of the proposed adaptive control algorithm.

articleTitle: Coexistence of 5G-FSS Analysis on Adjacent Channel Interference in Indonesia with LNB Replacement
publicationTitle: 2023 26th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The field test of the 5G-FSS coexistence has been conducted in Bandung, Indonesia. The 5G-FSS coexistence field test is conducted using an adjacent channel scheme between the services. The objective of the experiment is to analyze: (1) the impact of the unwanted signal source (interference) from the 5G service received by the fixed-satellite service (FSS), (2) the effect of additional Bandpass Filter (BPF) and Low Noise Block Downconverter (LNB) replacement to the performance of RF key parameters, (3) the interference level due to addition the number of 5G User Equipment (UE), transmit power of 5G Base Transceiver Station (BTS), and the guard band between the service. The result for both scenarios (Full C-Band LNB with BPF test and Standard C-Band LNB with BPF test) show that there is still leakage of unwanted signal from 5G services in the guard band and the Standard C-Band channel, which the FSS still occupies. It implies that the radio frequency (RF) key parameters of C/(I+N), observed in the field test of 5G-FSS coexistence, are significantly degraded compared to the baseline conditions without any changes on the FSS system. The degradation happens because the interference level received by the VSAT is increasing, and the rejection by adding BPF and replacing LNB with Standard C-Band LNB is still insufficient to overcome the high level of the interference signal.
